topic.name: The Cross Product of Two Vectors

question.text: The vector $\mathbf{a}$ has magnitude $7,$ the vector $\mathbf{b}$ has magnitude $3,$ the angle between $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ is $55^\circ$ and $\mathbf{n}$ is the unit vector that points in the direction of $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}.$ Find $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}$ in terms of $\mathbf{n}.$ Round your final answer to the nearest integer where appropriate.
question.explanation:
We use the formula for the cross product and obtain

\begin{align} \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} & = |\mathbf{a}| \cdot |\mathbf{b}| \cdot \sin{\theta} \cdot \mathbf{n} \\[3pt] & = 7 \cdot 3 \cdot \sin{55^\circ} \cdot\mathbf{n} \\[3pt] & = 21 (0.819 \ldots) \cdot \mathbf{n} \\[3pt] & = (17.202 \ldots) \cdot \mathbf{n}\\[3pt] & \approx 17 \mathbf{n}. \end{align}

example.title: Calculating the Cross Product of Two Vectors Whose Angle Is a Non-Special Angle

question.text: The vector $\mathbf{a}$ has magnitude $8$, the vector $\mathbf{b}$ has magnitude $3,$ the angle between $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ is $85^\circ$ and $\mathbf{n}$ is the unit vector that points in the direction of $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}.$ Find $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}$ in terms of $\mathbf{n}.$ Round your final answer to one decimal place where appropriate.
question.explanation:
We use the formula for the cross product and obtain

\[ \eqalign{ \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} &= |\mathbf{a}| \cdot |\mathbf{b}| \cdot \sin{\theta} \cdot \mathbf{n} \\[3pt] &= 8 \cdot 3 \cdot \sin{85^\circ} \cdot \mathbf{n} \\[3pt] & = 24 \cdot (0.996\,19 \ldots) \cdot \mathbf{n} \\[3pt] & = (23.908\,67 \ldots) \cdot \mathbf{n} \\[3pt] & \approx 23.9 \mathbf{n}. } \]

example.title: Calculating the Cross Product of Two Vectors Whose Angle Is a Non-Special Angle

question.text: The vector $\mathbf{a}$ has magnitude $5,$ the vector $\mathbf{b}$ has magnitude $2,$ and $\mathbf{a} \parallel \mathbf{b}.$ Find $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}.$
question.explanation:
Suppose $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ are nonzero vectors. Then, $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{0}$ if and only if $\mathbf{a} \parallel \mathbf{b}.$

Therefore, $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{0}.$
